components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single most important action per view (Create, Activate).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: oklch(0.6 0.2 260); color: oklch(0.98 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.6 0.2 260); border-radius: 0.425rem; padding: 0.375rem 0.875rem; font: 600 0.75rem/1.4 'Source Sans 3', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.52 0.2 260); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.6 0.2 260 / 0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Default secondary action; semantic variants tint border and text.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: oklch(0.93 0.005 260); border: 1px solid oklch(0.2 0.01 260); border-radius: 0.425rem; padding: 0.3125rem 0.875rem; font: 600 0.75rem/1.4 'Source Sans 3', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: oklch(0.6 0.2 260); color: oklch(0.6 0.2 260); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.6 0.2 260 / 0.5); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Environment/service state; text always names the state.
components.css: .ds-badge-running { display: inline-block; background: rgba(52, 211, 153, 0.12); color: #34d399; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; font: 600 0.6875rem/1.4 'Source Sans 3', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Environment Card
components.description: Resource row: title + badge left, actions right, mono metadata below.
components.css: .ds-card { background: oklch(0.1 0.01 260); border: 1px solid oklch(0.2 0.01 260); border-radius: 0.625rem; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; color: oklch(0.93 0.005 260); font-family: 'Source Sans 3', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.625rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-card-badge { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.12); color: #34d399; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-card-meta { font-size: 0.75rem; color: oklch(0.7 0.01 260); } .ds-card-meta code { font-family: 'Source Code Pro', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; color: oklch(0.93 0.005 260); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Form field on Console Field fill; focus ring is mandatory.

components.description: Section tab; active = Console Blue text + 2px underline.

narrative.overview: The dashboard is the working instrument behind oduflow.dev: the same deep blue-black console field, the same single confident blue power light, the same categorical signal palette — but tuned for an operator in a task, not a visitor on a tour. Where the site demonstrates the machine, the dashboard is the machine: status badges, container stats, sync output, and live terminals are the content, and the design's job is to keep them scannable at density. Hierarchy comes from weight and tonal steps on the blue-black ramp, never from decoration. This is product register: fixed rem type scale, one sans carrying every role through weight contrast, monospace as the native voice of machine artifacts, motion limited to 150-250ms state feedback.
keyCharacteristics: Blue-black console field with one confident Console Blue accent (≤15% of any screen)
Signal colors used categorically for state and channels, never decoratively
One humanist sans (Source Sans 3) + its companion mono (Source Code Pro), both self-hosted
Earned density: compact rows, full data, text contrast ≥4.5:1
Flat at rest; depth via tonal surface steps, shadows only as state response
Every asset ships with the package — no CDNs, ever

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Console Blue is the only brand accent that carries weight; ≤15% of any screen. Do not introduce a second "primary".

rules.name: The Channel Rule
rules.body: Signal colors are categorical. A color may mark a state or a capability channel; a surface never gets a signal color "for variety". If you can't name the channel, use neutral or Console Blue.

rules.name: The Defined Token Rule
rules.body: Every var(--*) reference must resolve to a token declared in :root. A reference to an undeclared custom property is a bug, not a fallback.

rules.name: The Console Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for what the machine produces or consumes: names, paths, images, output, counts. Never set UI copy in mono for flavor — and never set machine artifacts in the sans.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: At this density, hierarchy inside a card comes from weight (400 vs 600) and tone (Ink vs Muted Ink), not from adding type sizes. Five sizes total; do not invent a sixth.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A shadow on a resting element is a bug. Layering at rest is tonal: Field for the page, Surface for cards and bars, Subtle for fills inside cards.

rules.name: The Raised Edge Rule
rules.body: Every overlay (modal, menu, toast) gets the Raised Surface background and the Raised Hairline border. If an overlay's edge can't be traced against a dimmed page, it is missing one of the two.

dos: Do keep Console Blue at ≤15% of any screen; semantic action colors carry the rest of the meaning.
Do give every interactive component all five states (default, hover, focus-visible, disabled, loading); the focus ring is never removed.
Do set machine artifacts (DB names, images, paths, logs, counts) in Source Code Pro per The Console Voice Rule.
Do keep status badges textual; color reinforces, text informs.
Do ship every asset (fonts, xterm.js, css) inside the package — the dashboard must work air-gapped. A CDN <script> is a bug.
Do pair any animation (spinner, toast, usage bars) with a prefers-reduced-motion alternative.
Do declare every CSS custom property you reference (The Defined Token Rule).
donts: Don't import glossy SaaS landing grammar: no gradients, no gradient text, no glassmorphism, no marketing tone in UI copy.
Don't drift toward toy no-code styling: no oversized cards, no cartoon illustration, and no emoji as UI affordances (🔒/🔓 in buttons must become text or an inline SVG).
Don't keep GitHub-clone anonymity: #0d1117 / #58a6ff / #3fb950 is GitHub's palette, not Oduflow's. Migrate to the Console tokens.
Don't rebuild overloaded-enterprise clutter: an action row longer than ~5 buttons must split into primary actions + an overflow menu.
Don't hardcode hex values in JS or inline styles outside the token system (#7a1f1f, #1f4f7a, the ANSI map); promote them to named tokens.
Don't use native prompt()/confirm() as the long-term affordance for editing and destructive confirmation; replace with inline editing and a consistent confirm pattern when touched.
Don't animate layout properties; usage-bar fills animate transform: scaleX(), not width.
